names: Trail of Tears National Historic Trail

points.note: Pin is on the water side of the park in our map data, not checked against the water line. Walk to the water and set up inside the park within 100 ft of it.
The POTA location for Fort Heiman.

spots.note: Trail of Tears Water Route: the Tennessee River (Kentucky Lake). The trail here is the river itself, so set up on public land inside the park AND within 100 ft of the water. Kentucky Lake is the dammed Tennessee River; the NPS route line follows the old river channel out in the lake, so this is a looser fit than an Ohio River bank. Fort Heiman is a unit of Fort Donelson National Battlefield, so the same land counts for both. The pin is approximate and was not checked against the water line. Possible only: do your own research.

spots.note: Trail of Tears Water Route: the Tennessee River (Kentucky Lake), along the west side of Land Between the Lakes. The trail here is the river itself, so set up on public land inside the park AND within 100 ft of the water. Kentucky Lake is the dammed Tennessee River; the NPS route line follows the old river channel out in the lake, so this is a looser fit than an Ohio River bank. Any public LBL shore on the Kentucky Lake side may work; the Lake Barkley side is the Cumberland River and does not count. The pin is approximate and was not checked against the water line. Possible only: do your own research.

Ohio River Islands National Wildlife Refuge

points.what: Manchester Islands, Ohio River (approximate, boat only)
points.note: Land on Manchester 1 or 2 island; the whole island is within the trail corridor (the Ohio River). Nearest public ramp: Manchester, Ohio (Island Creek, SR 52).

spots.note: Ohio River: the Lewis & Clark route. The Kentucky part of the refuge is Manchester 1 and Manchester 2 islands (river mile 395), reached only by boat. Watch for steep banks and rock dikes when landing. Open 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset; no camping, fires or overnight mooring. The National Park Service also lists the refuge on its Lewis & Clark "Visitor Centers in Kentucky" page. Possible only: do your own research.

changes: Every park name now matches the POTA Kentucky park list exactly (no shortened or agency names such as "Outdoor Recreation Area", "Sunnybrook", "Burchell-Beech Creek" or "Peabody").
Every GPS pin is labeled as a guide that gets you to the area, not a confirmed activation spot.
Riverbank pins are marked approximate (grade C): they were not checked against the actual water line, and some may be more than 100 ft from the river.

The four historic trail sites now say plainly that they are NOT within 100 ft of the river or trail, and cite the National Park Service page each one relies on. Big Bone Lick is an NPS "High Potential Historic Site" and Wickliffe Mounds is on the NPS Lewis & Clark pages; neither is called a visitor center by the NPS.
Removed a Red River 3-fer pin that pointed to a spot 33 km outside the Daniel Boone National Forest, and a general Land Between the Lakes pin 7 mi from Golden Pond Visitor Center.
Moved 19 setup and trail pins that sat on or just outside a boundary line so they are at least 100 ft inside every park in our map data.
Parking pins say "Parking only" and note when the lot may be just outside the park line.
Pennyrile Forest State Park + Pennyrile State Forest: a KPC member confirmed they do not overlap, so it is NOT a 2-fer.

Added Trail of Tears Water Route spots on the Tennessee River (Kentucky Lake): Land Between the Lakes, Kentucky Lake WMA, Kenlake State Park, Kentucky Dam Village State Park and a Fort Heiman 3-fer; and on the Mississippi River: Doug Travis WMA. Checked against the NPS route map.
Added Livingston County WMA (Trail of Tears Northern Route runs through it). Columbus-Belmont: the NPS Benge Route runs through the park, so it now has an on-route pin.
Wickliffe Mounds, Big Bone Lick and Golden Pond now cite the NPS "Visitor Centers in Kentucky" page for the Lewis & Clark trail.

Lewis & Clark auto tour route: checked the NPS route for all of Kentucky. It runs along the edges of Big Bone Lick, Wickliffe Mounds, Otter Creek, Yellowbank WMA and Livingston County WMA; each now has a pin inside the park next to the signed route, and Livingston County WMA is a new possible Lewis & Clark 2-fer.
Added US-0608 Ohio River Islands National Wildlife Refuge (Manchester islands, Lewis County, boat only) as a possible Lewis & Clark 2-fer.

Sheltowee Trace + Big South Fork NRA: added the Yamacraw trail spot (KY 92 bridge, 36.725318, -84.543018, suggested by KZ4CP) and the KDFWR Yamacraw river access parking. Checked: not a 3-fer, the Big South Fork Wild River (US-10107) runs only from the Tennessee line to Blue Heron (POTA park notes and KY GIS).

planning: Use the spot cards in this guide or the trip routes below. Start with grade A and B spots; leave grade C (check satellite view) for when you have time to scout.
Build it in the KY Trip Planner

Open the KY Trip Planner on the KPC site, add each park as a stop and turn on Park Overlaps plus the Trail of Tears, Lewis & Clark and Lewis & Clark auto tour route layers. It draws the route, counts the miles and exports a GPX.
Check each park before you go

Open the official park map. Wildlife Management Areas have hunting seasons (wear blaze orange in gun seasons), some lots and gates close, and national forest spots count only on Forest Service-owned land.
Riverbank and Kentucky Lake shore pins are approximate. Look at satellite view for a public place within 100 ft of the water. Trail spots must be within 100 ft of the trail and inside the other park.
Historic trails: look for the sign

POTA's Activator Guide says historic trails have no specific boundaries, so you need an NPS-certified site or official signage. Take a photo of the brown Lewis and Clark Trail / AUTO TOUR ROUTE or Trail of Tears sign at your spot.
Spot every reference you are activating, log each park separately (one log file per park) and keep your whole station inside every park. Upload each log to POTA after the trip.

Radio, battery, antenna that fits a small footprint, 100 ft of string or a tape to check the 100 ft rule, blaze orange in hunting season, water, a paper map (cell service is poor in the gorge and along the rivers).
